title: Tooling backlog: how agents build this repo (not product features)

items.title: Spec pipeline: tester -> coder -> reviewer loop driven by a script
items.idea: A script takes a spec folder (specs/NNN-name/) and walks tasks.md. Per task: tester writes failing tests from the spec; a test reviewer checks them against the spec (optional); coder edits code until tests and linters are green; a code reviewer checks the code against the spec and sends findings back to the coder; the tester then strengthens the tests (edge cases) and red tests go back to the coder; commit, next task; one PR per spec, reviewed by the coordinator.
design_notes: Roles run as headless Claude Code (claude -p) with a model per role (e.g. coder DeepSeek, reviewer Sonnet); same mechanism as the DeepSeek runs of 2026-10-24.
The script, not the model, enforces role limits by git diff: a coder change under tests/ or a tester change under src/ is rolled back.
Tests before code need named interfaces: specs written for the pipeline list exact modules, functions and signatures.
Hard caps per task (iterations) and per run (tokens or money; proposed $2 per spec for paid models); on a cap the script stops and reports.
Prior art to reuse: .codex/skills/multi-agent-orchestration/scripts/run_executor_reviewer.sh (Codex executor/reviewer, not in use).
First run: a small backlog item (F1 pipeline findings) to measure cost and how many findings the coordinator's review still finds.
open_questions: Budget per run (proposed $2 for DeepSeek) - owner.
Spec number: next free under specs/ when started.

items.title: Refactor complex, duplicated and dead code found by crapper, dryer and mutator
items.decided: Owner 2026-11-01: valid point, keep as a backlog task; new code is checked per PR (advisory), old code is cleaned here, not inside feature PRs.

facts_2026_11_01.tools: unclebob crapper, dryer, mutator installed manually in ~/tools/unclebob on the owner's Mac (not in CI); Python supported.
facts_2026_11_01.crapper_no_coverage_on_src: about 100 functions with cyclomatic complexity >= 10 (coverage not measured, so real CRAP scores unknown)
facts_2026_11_01.dryer_on_src: 9 duplicate pairs with score >= 0.9, e.g. src/app/storage/source_repo.py:164-176 vs src/app/storage/source_candidate_repo.py:111-123; src/app/core/sources/onboarding.py:288-295 vs src/app/storage/source_repo.py:232-239; src/app/core/jev.py:35-43 vs src/app/core/sources/review.py:138-142

steps: Run crapper with coverage (`crapper --use-existing-coverage` after a pytest coverage run) to get real CRAP scores; list functions with CRAP >= 10.
Group findings by module; one small PR per module or duplicate pair, behavior pinned by tests first (AGENTS.md test-first rule), reviewed by another session.
Start with the 9 dryer pairs (cheap, low risk), then the worst CRAP functions in ingestion and daily signals.

Dead code: find code nothing calls (coverage report lines never hit, `vulture src` as a hint, mutator uncovered sites); for each candidate check callers (CLI, systemd scripts, tests, dynamic imports) before deleting; one PR per area, each deletion listed with its reason. Owner asked for this 2026-11-01.
Optionally run mutator on one critical module (e.g. src/app/core/world/filter.py) to judge test strength; full-project mutator runs take hours.
items.done_when: No dryer pair >= 0.8 in src/ and no function with CRAP >= 30; remaining 10-30 cases listed with a reason; dead-code candidates either deleted or listed with the reason they stay.
items.done: 2026-11-01: 15 plan rows plus 7b, 11a/11b as PRs #170-#186 (except #174, #185 docs), each reviewed by another agent with mutation checks, merged after green CI. Dead code removed; dryer groups A, C, D gone; complexity of the target functions cut (e.g. _screen_candidate 25->7, _process_html_links_two_stage 34->14, run_fetch_cycle 25->8, parse_summary 21->4); characterization tests added before every split. Plan, log and prompts: docs/archive/2026-11/plan-t2-refactor-2026-11-01.md, t2-log-2026-11-01.md.
left_out: JavaScript in src/app/web/static (no JS test harness; separate task if wanted)
FastAPI route factories and 100%-covered rule code (high CC is structure, not risk)

items.title: Pick the executor (model and effort) per task: a rule table first, Jev as a router later
items.idea: The coordinator does too much itself and has no rule for choosing between Codex (Sol/Astra, efforts), DeepSeek, Haiku, Sonnet and itself. Step 1: a rule table in the coordinator rules. Step 2 (only if the table misses): Jev reads the task description and returns model, effort and one line why.

draft_table.coordinator itself: mechanical edits, git, merge, fact checks
draft_table.Haiku: running tools, log digging, production summaries (read-only)
draft_table.Codex Astra high: code review (always a model other than the author)

open_questions: Jev router: one paid call per task; check it on past tasks against the choices actually made before trusting it.
